evidence.quote: we begin with firms making annual capex forecasts (as covered by IBES) and match these firms to Compustat using the IBES linkfile. This gives us an initial sample of 40,785 forecasts between the years 2002 and 2016
Matching these forecasts with CRSP to obtain short-window market reaction (on the issuance date) reduces the sample to 36,900 forecasts.
We delete 17,473 forecasts that are made concurrently with an earnings forecast and another 1,850 that are made in 2016 because we need actual capital expenditure data as of the end of the year.
The final sample comprises 17,577 capex forecasts made by 1,790 unique firms over the period 2003 to 2015.
Our unit of observation in most tables is a firm-quarter.

evidence.quote: The dependent variable is capex adjustments (CAPEX_ADJ) defined as the percentage deviation of actual capex from forecasted capex scaled by the latter.

items.label: Key independent variable(s)
value: CAR: cumulative abnormal return (firm return minus S&P500 index return) over the 5 days surrounding the capex forecast date; standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
SF_CAR: market reaction to sales forecasts made for the same fiscal period and closest to the capex forecast; standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
MKTRET: market returns on the forecast date; standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation
CAR_PRE: pseudo-market reactions around a nonforecast date; standardized to zero mean and unit standard deviation

evidence.quote: CAR, defined as the cumulative abnormal return (i.e., firm return minus S&P500 index return) over the 5 days surrounding the capex forecast date (i.e., days [-2, 2] relative to the forecast date).
SF_CAR denotes market reaction to sales forecasts made for the same fiscal period and closest to the capex forecast.
MKTRET denotes market returns on the forecast date. CAR_PRE denotes pseudo-market reactions around a nonforecast date.
CAR, SF_CAR, MKTRET, and CAR_PRE have been standardized to have zero means and unit standard deviations.
